summary_for_children: Al-Muzzammil calls to stand at night in prayer and to recite the Quran slowly and beautifully.
environment_concept: A dial of the night hours (73:2-4) and a reading stand for slow, measured recitation (73:4).
architecture_and_scenery: A house with a night window and a sky dial showing parts of the night.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A flat-roofed village at sunset with a quiet roof terrace and a tall water clock that empties from sunset to dawn

primary_mechanic.text: Tonight runs from 18:30 to 05:00 (10.5 hours). Set pegs on the water clock for a third (22:00), half (23:45) and two thirds (01:30) of the night, in 15-minute steps; a wrong time is refused as too early or too late. Then keep watch as the water falls past each peg (73:2-4, 73:20).

secondary_activities: the hours of the night (73:6-8, read)
unique_world.narrative_structure: Two readings on the way up, then the water clock through the night
environment_behaviour: pegs appear on the clock as they are set
the water level falls through the watch
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that Allah measures the night and the day, and that we recite what is easy (73:20)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Quiet Night
story_library.children_narration: When the world becomes quiet at night, it can be easier to concentrate and reflect. Surah Al-Muzzammil emphasizes night prayer, reciting the Quran carefully, and remembering Allah. It also recognizes that people have different responsibilities and circumstances.

world_idea.title: The Night Observatory
world_idea.description: Experience a calm transition from evening to dawn and learn about thoughtful Quran recitation and the passage of time.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
